findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are hardcoded in plaintext in the instance user_data script, which is readable by anyone with DescribeInstances/console access and is stored unencrypted in the instance metadata and Terraform state.
No metadata_options block is set to require IMDSv2 (http_tokens = required), leaving the legacy instance metadata service enabled and vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true (and the setting is explicitly commented out), leaving data at rest on the volume unencrypted.
The EBS snapshot inherits the unencrypted state of the source volume, meaning snapshot data at rest is also unencrypted and could be shared or restored without protection.
The security group allows inbound TCP port 22 (SSH) from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing administrative access to the entire internet.

The security group allows inbound TCP port 80 from 0.0.0.0/0; while web traffic is often public, combined with unrestricted egress and no compensating controls this widens the attack surface unnecessarily.
The security group allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel from the instance.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads that may not need direct internet reachability.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true automatically assigns public IP addresses to instances in this subnet, increasing exposure of workloads that may not need direct internet reachability.

findings.issue_category: missing encryption and public access controls
findings.description: The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration and no public access block, and force_destroy is enabled, risking unencrypted log data and potential unauthorized access or accidental data loss.
